_source.title: 事故防止に係る総点検の実施結果（運行計画）
_source.publisher: 国土交通省 (Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism)
what_it_is: An official MLIT survey of Japanese railway operators, conducted after the
2005 Fukuchiyama Line derailment, asking each operator how it builds margin
into its operating plan. Two columns matter here:
駅間での余裕のとり方 - how margin is added to interstation running time
停車時の余裕のとり方 - how margin is added to station dwell time
This is the single most valuable source in the project. It documents, from
the regulator, the operational policy that this simulation is trying to
measure from the outside. Without it the gap between simulation and
timetable would be attributable only by hand-waving.

jr_east._note: JR East's own entry, verbatim in substance. It describes the practice but states no numbers for the Yamanote.

practice: Run curves (運転曲線図) are drawn accounting for vehicle performance,
track conditions, line usage conditions, and driveability (運転操縦性).
The run time computed from that curve is BASICALLY ROUNDED UP to become
the standard run time (基準運転時分).
Separately, when the timetable is built, necessary margin time (余裕時分)

quantified_example.note: Not the Yamanote, but the only JR East figure the document quantifies.

interstation_margin.implication: The published timetable sits at least three layers above the theoretical minimum: de-rated run curve, then round-up, then added margin.

dwell.practice: Set from operating results (実績) and on-site surveys (現地調査). Extended at high-traffic stations according to time of day.
dwell.note: JR East does not publish a base dwell figure. This is the gap that peer-operator figures below are used to bracket.

speed_derating_by_operator._note: Operators that state they draw the run curve BELOW the actual speed limit. This is the clearest evidence that the industry baseline run time is not the theoretical minimum. JR East states the practice qualitatively but gives no number, so the peer range is applied as a modelled assumption.
speed_derating_by_operator._unit: km/h below the posted speed limit

voltage_derating_by_operator._note: Operators that additionally draw the run curve at reduced catenary voltage, which lowers available acceleration. Not attributed to JR East; recorded because it shows how conservative the industry baseline is.

dwell_by_operator_seconds._note: Stated base dwell times. Used to bracket the Yamanote, which is at the busy extreme of this set. Figures are as published by each operator in the MLIT survey.

Seibu.note: extended further at high-volume stations and trains

Tokyo_Metro.basis: computed from boarding/alighting numbers and door open/close time, plus margin
